summary: Recolour the connected region (same original colour, 4-directional) containing a starting pixel.
mainInsight: Starting from the pixel, recursively recolour every connected pixel that has the original colour. If the new colour equals the original, return immediately - otherwise the recolouring cannot mark pixels as visited and recursion never ends.

approaches.name: DFS
approaches.summary: Recolour and recurse into matching neighbours.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal; the early return for original == color is essential.

options: DFS/BFS over connected cells with the same colour
Binary search over the pixel colour values
Sorting the pixels by their current colour
Dynamic programming over the grid cells
cards.answer: DFS/BFS over connected cells with the same colour
cards.explanation: The region is defined by connectivity and equal colour.

promptVariants: Why does recolouring double as the visited marker, and when does that fail?
Why return early when original == color?
cards.answer: Changing a pixel to the new colour means it no longer equals the original colour, so the DFS naturally skips it later (no separate visited set). If the new colour equals the original, recolouring changes nothing, so pixels would be revisited forever; the early return avoids that.
cards.explanation: Same trick as Number of Islands.
Each pixel is processed at most once.

promptVariants: What is the worst-case recursion depth?
How deep can the Flood Fill recursion get, and what avoids the recursion limit?
cards.answer: O(m n) when the region snakes through the whole image; BFS or an explicit stack avoids the recursion limit.

promptVariants: What happens when the new colour equals the starting pixel's colour?
Why is that a special case?
options: Return the image unchanged to avoid infinite recursion
Recolour every pixel in the grid to 0 first
Raise an error because nothing would change
Recolour only the start pixel and stop there
cards.answer: Return the image unchanged to avoid infinite recursion
cards.explanation: Nothing would be marked as visited, so the DFS would revisit pixels without end.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Recolour only the start pixel and stop t: It would not mark neighbours either.
